user_input:
Super Intelligence App
A biologically-inspired multi-agent system whose architecture mirrors the human brain. Clusters of switch neurons (cheap, deterministic) and integrator agents (LLM, expensive) produce conversational behaviour. Intelligence emerges from wiring, modulation, and memory — not from a single orchestrator.

See PLAN.md for the original design doc and brain/CONSTITUTION.md for the philosophical commitments.

Quick start
# One-shot launch (Ollama + brain + browser UI with all features)
./start.sh
Then visit http://localhost:8765.

The first run will pull Ollama models (qwen2.5:7b, nomic-embed-text) and may take a few minutes. Subsequent runs reuse cached models.

Prerequisites
Tool	Why	Install
uv	Python env + dep manager	curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Ollama	Local LLM + embeddings	brew install ollama
API keys	Cloud LLM, voice	See .env.example
Copy .env.example → .env and fill in the keys you have. Anthropic + Google are needed for the cloud integrators; Deepgram + ElevenLabs only when voice mode is on; Langfuse is optional (the local decisions log works without it).

Launch modes
start.sh takes a FEATURES env-var preset:

./start.sh                       # full stack (default)
FEATURES=standard ./start.sh     # UI + DMN + metacognition + motor (no voice)
FEATURES=minimal ./start.sh      # text-only UI
FEATURES=custom BRAIN_EXTRA_ARGS="--ui --voice" ./start.sh
Full stack enables:

--ui — browser at :8765
--voice — Deepgram streaming mic + ElevenLabs TTS
--ears — auditory cortex (speaker enrollment, prosody, song fingerprint)
--dmn — Default Mode Network: idle thinking every 15 s
--metacognition — self-monitoring cell: reflects on behaviour every 30 s
--motor — tool use (file I/O + shell commands, sandboxed to BRAIN_MOTOR_PATHS)
You can also run brain.run directly with any subset of those flags. CLI flags and BRAIN_* env vars are equivalent.

Architecture at a glance
PNS ──► sensory.text ──► Temporal ──► Hypothalamus ──► Frontal ──► Brainstem ──► PNS
                       │             │              │           (articulation)
                       └► Hippocampus│              │
                                     └► Parietal ───┘
                                                    │
                                              Motor Cortex
Each cluster has:

Switch neurons (brain/neuron.py) — deterministic code, cheap, the connective tissue. ~80% excitatory, ~20% inhibitory.
Integrator cells (brain/cell.py) — LLM-backed, fire only at convergence zones where reasoning genuinely needs to happen.
Predictor (brain/predictor.py) — anticipates the cluster's output; integrators stay asleep on low surprise. Emotion-aware veto forces integrators awake when the entity or user is in a non-routine emotional state.
Hebbian edge weights (brain/wiring.py) — connections between cells/clusters carry weights nudged by outcome at sleep consolidation. Weighted routing decides which drafters fire, which temporal switches evaluate first, and how memory recall fans out.
Long-term state lives in second_brain/:

schema/self.md, schema/user.md — human-readable, hand-editable; routed per recognised speaker
episodes/episodes.lance/ — vector-indexed turn summaries
episodes/procedures.lance/ — procedural memory (muscle memory)
wiring.json — Hebbian edge weights (persists across sessions)
wiring_history/{session_id}.json — per-session snapshots for evolution charting
Signal model
Neuromodulators (fast, per-turn)
Signal	Role
DA	Reward / positive valence
ACh	Curiosity, attentional engagement
GABA	Inhibition, de-escalation
Glu	General arousal, salience
NE	Focused alertness — sharp attentional spotlight, rises with surprise and threat
Hormonal channels (slow, session-level)
Signal	Role
OXT	Oxytocin — builds on warm exchange; buffers CORT
CORT	Cortisol — sustained social-threat accumulation
5HT	Serotonin — slow lift from rewarding interaction
AEA	Anandamide — homeostatic buffer; rises when Glu+NE arousal exceeds threshold; antagonised by CORT
Hormonal channels decay on a time-weighted wall-clock schedule, not per-turn. OXT and AEA cross-antagonise CORT. Hormonal state is shown in the browser UI and logged to Langfuse.

Continuous affect dimensions
Hypothalamus maps the neuromodulator state to continuous valence and arousal dimensions before naming an emotion. This separates the two axes of Russell's circumplex model and prevents the emotion label from being the only signal downstream clusters receive.

Predict-and-surprise gating
Active Inference applied at cluster level: each integrator has a predictor that fires first. If surprise is low, the integrator stays asleep.

Gate	What it guards
PredictorSwitch in Temporal	skips understanding integrator on routine input
CompositePredictor in Frontal	skips executive when response shape is predictable; skips critic when past scores on similar shapes were consistently high
Encoder gate in Hippocampus	skips LLM summarisation on low-surprise/low-DA turns; episode still stored
Recall reuse	near-identical recall queries reuse the previous result
Emotion-aware veto bypasses gating when high_GABA, when the entity's emotion is reactive (angry, defensive, frustrated, sympathetic, etc.), when the user's emotion needs care (distressed, sad, hostile, etc.), or when the vocal tone is stressed/whisper.

Hebbian wiring
Composite outcome signal: 0.5 * DA_delta + 0.3 * critic_score + 0.2 * user_emotion_delta

Plasticity modulator scales the learning rate by session-averaged DA + ACh (sad/flat sessions learn slowly; engaged sessions learn faster)
Homeostatic decay (1% toward resting weight 1.0) prevents lock-in
Tendency-match bonus reinforces coherence between emotional state and behavioural choice
Updates applied at sleep consolidation; weights consulted live for drafter selection, switch ordering, and recall fan-out (ε-greedy exploration)
Skip rules: outcome too small (|outcome| < 0.05), turn was a defuse response, or entity was confused/flat with negative user emotion.

Frontal subsystem architecture
The frontal lobe dispatches to pluggable FrontalSubsystem implementations (brain/clusters/frontal_subsystem.py). The executive runs first and classifies intent; the first matching subsystem handles it; conversational drafting (Multiple Drafts engine) is the fallback.

Current subsystems:

Subsystem	Trigger	What it does
FrontalTaskSubsystem	requires_action=True	Extracts goal → deposits in PendingTask for motor cortex
To add a subsystem: implement FrontalSubsystem, register it in FrontalCluster.__init__.

FollowThrough (SMA loop)
brain/clusters/follow_through.py — after the drafter finalises a response, this module detects spoken commitments ("let me grab that", "I'll go check") and re-queues them as synthetic self-directed turns. The executive then classifies the turn as a task and the motor cortex executes it. This closes the loop between intention and action without requiring an external trigger.

Motor cortex
Tool use is sandboxed to BRAIN_MOTOR_PATHS. Motor cortex supports pluggable MotorSubsystem implementations (brain/clusters/motor_subsystem.py):

before_plan() — inject context into the planner prompt
recall_procedure() — check procedural memory for a high-confidence prior
predict_outcome() — forward model: predict tool-call output before execution
after_job() — record completed jobs for learning
Muscle memory (ProcedureStore)
brain/clusters/motor_memory.py — completed motor jobs are stored as vector-indexed procedures in second_brain/episodes/ (same LanceDB database as episodic memory, separate table). On subsequent similar tasks:

Above _SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD (0.75): prior steps are prepended as context
Above _OPEN_LOOP_THRESHOLD (0.90) with ≥2 prior successes: motor runs the procedure without LLM re-planning (open-loop execution)
The cloud executor (brain/clusters/cloud_executor.py) has WebSearch and WebFetch tools enabled for cloud-side tool calls.

Skill injection
brain/skill_loader.py reads .md files from brain/skills/ and injects them into system prompts for local (Ollama) model calls only. Cloud calls are unaffected. To add a skill: drop a .md file in brain/skills/. To clone a skill from your Claude Code installation: python brain/skill_loader.py clone <name>.

Auditory cortex and speaker routing
With --ears enabled:

Speaker enrollment — voice fingerprints are registered on first contact
Per-speaker schema routing — each recognised speaker gets their own schema/user_<id>.md; unknown voices fall back to schema/user.md
Prosody extraction — pitch, pace, voice features extracted and logged to Langfuse
Response-length mirroring — the brain roughly matches its output length to the user's input length
Song fingerprint — detects music in the audio stream
Image pipeline
Upload images via the browser UI (/upload_image). Occipital cortex passes them to a VLM integrator; the description is injected into the drafter context.

Default Mode Network
With --dmn:

Idle thoughts fire every ~8 s during conversation, ~25 s when the OS reports the user is idle
Bidirectional coupling: DMN thoughts influence neuromodulator state; neuromodulator state gates DMN firing
Feedback loops: thoughts can re-trigger downstream emotion/memory updates
Thought deduplication: near-duplicate thoughts are suppressed; recent unique thoughts are surfaced
Idle gate: DMN is suppressed when the brain is actively processing user input
Observability
Everything routes through one append-only JSONL stream + the browser UI. Three record types in eval/turns.jsonl:

Type	What
turn	Full TurnTrace (response, emotion, neuromod, draft scores, fired_path, predictor_outcomes, llm_calls_saved)
decision	Every predict-and-surprise and Hebbian decision with the reason
eval_patch	Async patches from baseline runner / post-hoc scorer
Decision flavours include:

skip_executive_integrator / skip_critic / skip_temporal_integrator / skip_encoder / reuse_recent_recall
gate_bypassed_emotional (with bypass reason)
weighted_drafter_selection (picked drafter, weights, ε-greedy roll, divergence flag)
weighted_switch_order, weighted_recall_fanout
hebbian_update_applied (per-edge with from/to weight + delta)
hebbian_update_skipped (with reason)
session_plasticity_summary (session totals, top gainers/losers)
Tail the decisions stream
tail -f eval/turns.jsonl | jq 'select(.type=="decision")'
Browser UI (http://localhost:8765)
Neural Map — live wiring graph showing cluster activations and edge weights
Plasticity panel — cumulative LLM calls saved, predictor accuracy (rolling 50), plasticity modulator, top edges with session deltas, colour-coded decisions feed, [FROZEN] tag when BRAIN_WIRING_FROZEN=true
Neuromodulator panel — live DA, ACh, GABA, Glu, NE bars
Hormonal panel — live OXT, CORT, 5HT, AEA bars with time-decay visualisation
Activity log — left panel, per-turn event stream
Session learning evaluation
eval/learning_monitor.py — structural learning metrics computed from TurnTrace data without an LLM. Per-turn scores sent to Langfuse (learning.predictor_accuracy, learning.gating_efficiency, learning.avg_surprise, etc.). Session summary: predictor accuracy trend, gating efficiency trend, surprise trend, Hebbian edge change count and magnitude, cross-session weight drift.

Eval comparison
uv run python -m eval.compare
Buckets recent turns by whether gating fired (proxied via llm_calls_saved > 0 or gating_bypassed_count > 0) and reports avg LLM calls per turn + quality delta. Pass criterion: ≥25% call reduction with no statistically significant quality drop.

Escape hatches
BRAIN_WIRING_FROZEN=true — disables weighted routing everywhere. Hebbian learning still runs at sleep so weights accumulate. Use if behaviour drifts strangely.
BRAIN_DISABLE_PREDICT_GATING=true — forces every integrator to wake regardless of predictor confidence. For A/B eval comparisons.
Edit second_brain/wiring.json directly to nudge or zero specific edges. Bootstrap is idempotent — re-adding an existing edge is a no-op.
Edit second_brain/schema/self.md or user.md directly. Sleep consolidation rewrites only specific sections (History summary, Stable preferences); your other edits stick.
Testing
uv run pytest                                           # full suite (656+)
uv run pytest tests/test_predictor_gating.py            # predictor + bypass helper
uv run pytest tests/test_hebbian_pass.py                # wiring + sleep Hebbian pass
uv run pytest tests/test_decisions_log.py               # decisions → disk + UI
uv run pytest tests/test_motor_cortex.py                # motor cortex + muscle memory
uv run pytest tests/test_hormonal_system.py             # endocrine channels

user_input:
# Colony-Inspired Communication & Learning Capabilities

## Context

A scite literature pull (honey-bee/social-insect chemical communication, 2025) surfaced five findings that map cleanly onto this codebase's pheromone-like bus (`brain/bus.py`) and switch-neuron firing/learning (`brain/neuron.py`, `brain/hebbian.py`). The biology suggests concrete upgrades to how signals aggregate, how received signals gate learning, and how the colony specializes. This plan translates all five into the existing architecture, **gated behind a single master toggle** so they can be turned on as a bloc ("non-brain / colony-level capabilities") and A/B'd against the eval harness and persona traces before becoming default.

Three further phases push the synthesis further: Phase 6 ties the Bus concentration model into the existing memory/DMN systems so that *silent periods trigger recall* (hippocampal replay during quiescence; depends on Phase 2); Phase 7 unifies recruitment (Phase 4) and threshold diversity (Phase 5) into a single graded, self-limiting *resource-mobilization cascade* — the response-threshold model of division of labor — generalized beyond threats to any need (depends on Phases 4 & 5); Phase 8 adds a clamped feedback term so global neuromodulation adjusts to the system's own *aggregate cluster activity* (self-referential chemistry; highest-risk feedback loop, ships last). The three feedback loops are introduced in increasing-risk order (2 → 7 → 8), each enabled only after the prior is shown stable.

Guiding principle throughout: **reuse the existing machinery** (the modulator/`effective_threshold` system, the neuromod/hormonal layers, the `mem.recall`→hippocampus path, the DMN idle loop, the decisions log, the settings pattern) rather than introduce parallel systems. Each feature must be a no-op when the toggle is off, reproducing baseline behavior exactly.

**Note on Phase 1:** a literature check (three-factor learning rules + the inverted-U of stress on memory — see References) found the current *binary* plasticity skip to be biologically incorrect, so Phase 1 (graded plasticity) is reclassified as a **correctness fix on its own flag, deployed independently of the colony toggle**, not as an experimental colony feature.

Source papers — colony features (all 2025, OA): Giurfa (TiCS 29:979); Carroll et al. (PLOS ONE 20:e0317668); Mondet et al. & Gryboś et al. (releaser/primer); Ramírez-Moreno et al. (RSTB 380:1922). Plasticity basis: see References.

---

## Phase 0 — Master toggle

**File:** `brain/settings.py` (DEFAULTS dict, ~lines 22–434)

- Add `"colony_features": False` to `DEFAULTS`. This is the first **bool** default — note `Settings._load`/`update` coerce via `type(DEFAULTS[k])(v)`; JSON `true`/`false` deserialize to Python bools so coercion is safe. **Do not** store it as a string in `settings.json` (`bool("false")` is `True`).
- **Phase 1 is NOT under this toggle.** It ships on its own flag `"graded_plasticity": True` (a correctness fix, see Phase 1) plus its tuning keys `plasticity_turn_min/max` and a high-stress knee threshold. Validated and deployed independently of the colony bloc.
- Add per-feature tuning sub-settings (used only when the master flag is on), defaulting to neutral values:
  - `colony_conc_half_life_s: 45.0` (concentration/recruitment decay)
  - `colony_quorum_threshold: 1.5`, `colony_silence_floor: 0.15`
  - `colony_turn_plasticity_min: 0.4`, `colony_turn_plasticity_max: 1.3`
  - `colony_primer_gain: 0.3`, `colony_recruit_gain: 0.4`
  - `colony_threshold_spread: 0.08`
- Every behavior below checks `settings.get("colony_features", False)` at its entry point. Off ⇒ identical to today.

**Implication:** one switch flips the whole colony layer. Per-feature sub-settings let you tune without re-plumbing. Because each path is guarded, the eval baseline is byte-stable with the flag off.

---

## Phase 1 — Graded plasticity *(CORRECTNESS FIX — not colony-gated; `brain/hebbian.py`)*

**Status / why separated:** literature review (see References) establishes that the current *binary* `defuse_path` skip is **biologically wrong**, not merely unrefined. The graded replacement is the textbook model, so this phase is reclassified as a **correctness fix with its own flag** (`graded_plasticity`, default on after eval), **deployed independently of the experimental `colony_features` toggle.** It is still eval-gated (it changes learning dynamics — A/B against persona traces) but should not be bundled with the speculative colony work.

**Basis:**
- **Graded, neuromodulator-scaled plasticity = the three-factor learning rule** (Frémaux & Gerstner, 2016; Gerstner et al., 2018): weight change = pre × post × a neuromodulatory third factor that *continuously scales* learning. The existing DA+ACh `_plasticity_modulator` (hebbian.py:62) is already a (session-level) three-factor rule — that part is correct. Neuromodulation can even **flip the sign** of plasticity (Ang et al., 2021), so a binary on/off is far too coarse.
- **Aversive/threat states follow an inverted-U, not an off-switch** (Lukšys & Sandi, 2011; Kim et al., 2015; Rezayof et al., 2022): moderate arousal *facilitates* consolidation; only high stress impairs; and **emotionally intense events — including aversive ones — are encoded *more* strongly** (fear learning). The current `gaba_skip` (hebbian.py:71) is doubly wrong: it zeroes learning biology would only dampen, and it suppresses the high-salience aversive moments that should imprint hardest.

**Today:** `_plasticity_modulator` (hebbian.py:62) is a *session-averaged* DA+ACh scalar applied uniformly to every turn's `delta` (hebbian.py:193); the aversive side is a *binary* skip in `_should_skip_hebbian` (hebbian.py:71).

**Change — corrected, arousal-keyed mapping (NOT a simple valence ramp):**

- New method `_turn_plasticity(self, trace) -> float`, keyed primarily to **arousal / emotional intensity**, not valence sign:
  - Drivers (all already tracked per turn): ACh + NE + surprise/salience and DA swing (`da_delta`, hebbian.py:38–41) raise plasticity; **emotional *intensity* `|valence|`** (via `valence_of(trace.emotion)`/`user_emotion`, emotion_hierarchy.py:148) raises it for *either* sign — so intense aversive turns imprint hard (fear-learning case), not soft.
  - **Inverted-U high-stress knee:** only *very high* CORT/GABA pulls plasticity down (the descending limb); moderate stress does not. This replaces the binary skip.
  - Map to `[plasticity_turn_min, plasticity_turn_max]`.
- In `run` (hebbian.py:193): `delta = outcome * hebbian_outcome_delta * plasticity * turn_plast` when `graded_plasticity` on.
- Replace the binary `defuse_path` skip with the graded high-stress dampener (low, not zero). Keep `outcome_near_zero` and `dissociated_emotion` hard skips (those are signal-quality gates, not learning-rate claims).
- Telemetry: add `turn_plasticity` to `hebbian_update_applied` (hebbian.py:212) and a session aggregate in `session_plasticity_summary` (hebbian.py:257).

**Implication:** learning becomes graded at turn granularity along the *correct* axis — high-arousal/high-stakes moments (good **or** bad) imprint hard, flat moments imprint soft, and only extreme stress dampens — matching three-factor + inverted-U neuroscience instead of the current flat multiplier + all-or-nothing skip. Because it ships on its own flag, it can be validated and turned on without waiting on the colony features. Risk: the inverted-U knee location is a tuning parameter — start conservative (knee high) and move it with eval evidence.

---

## Phase 2 — Topic concentration / quorum + silence-as-signal *(headline; `brain/bus.py`)*

**Biology (Carroll et al. 2025):** brood-pheromone signal strength ≈ *summed concentration* across many producers (a colony census); the colony reacts to the **aggregate**, not individual emissions (quorum). And the *absence* of brood pheromone is itself a potent signal — it drives cannibalism; synthetic supplementation reverses it.

**Today (verified):** the Bus is pure fire-and-forget. `Bus.publish` (bus.py:222) fans out each `Message` and returns early on `msg.expired` (bus.py:223); expired messages are *silently dropped* (bus.py:201). There is **no per-topic state whatsoever** — no concentration, no last-seen timestamp, no record that a topic ever fired. A cluster therefore cannot distinguish "this topic went quiet" from "this topic has never spoken"; both are an empty queue. **Silence is currently invisible, and that is the hard part of this phase, not the accumulation.**

**Scope decision (per review):** this is the biggest architectural shift of the five, so **prototype it on ONE high-stakes channel first — threat/alarm detection — not bus-wide.** Prove the silence semantics there before generalizing. The mechanism is written generally but only *armed* for the threat channel in this phase.

**Phase 2 steps:**

1. **Identify the threat channel.** Confirm the concrete topic carrying threat/alarm signal (candidates: a threat-tagged signal, `attention.focus`, or the GABA component of `affect.state`). Pick exactly one; everything below is scoped to it.
2. **Concentration accumulator** on `Bus` (general, but only updated for the armed channel): `self._concentration: dict[str,float]`, `self._conc_ts: dict[str,float]`. On publish (toggle on, armed topic only): `concentration[topic] += msg.confidence`, with a cap to bound chatty topics. **Forward-compat for Phase 6:** also keep a tiny per-topic *associated-context* ring (last few messages' tags/entities + a neuromod snapshot) captured during the high-concentration window, so silence can later recall "what was going on," not just the topic name.
3. **Lazy decay read** `concentration(topic) -> float`: exp-decay since `_conc_ts[topic]` using `colony_conc_half_life_s`, update ts, return level.
4. **Explicit silence state machine** — the crux. A per-topic status: `UNARMED` (cold start — never reached threshold) → `ARMED` (concentration crossed an arm threshold at least once) → `QUIET` (was ARMED, then decayed below `colony_silence_floor`). Only `QUIET` counts as silence-as-signal; `UNARMED` never does. Define **reset/disarm semantics** explicitly: a topic disarms back to UNARMED after a long dwell at zero (so a one-time burst long ago doesn't make permanent silence "meaningful"). Decay below floor while ARMED = signal; absence while UNARMED = noise.
   - `quorum(topic) -> bool`: ARMED and `concentration >= colony_quorum_threshold`.
   - `is_quiet(topic) -> bool`: status == QUIET (never true from cold start).
5. **One wired consumer** on the threat channel only — e.g. hypothalamus/DMN reads `is_quiet(threat_topic)` ("threat that was present has now cleared → stand down") and/or `quorum(threat_topic)` ("sustained threat → collective caution"). Generalizing to other topics is explicitly deferred to a later, separate change.

**Implication:** the bus gains a stigmergic, quorum-sensing dimension and — the powerful part — the ability to treat *deliberate quiet* as information, **without** mistaking cold start for silence. Reuses the exp-decay idea already in `Neuromodulators.decay`. Risks: (a) unbounded accumulation → bounded by decay + cap; (b) the UNARMED/ARMED/QUIET semantics are the real design surface and must be unit-tested for every transition before trusting `is_quiet` anywhere. Off ⇒ accumulator never written; scoped-on ⇒ only the one threat channel is armed.

---

## Phase 3 — Releaser + primer in one message *(`brain/bus.py` + `brain/clusters/hypothalamus.py`)*

**Biology (Mondet/Gryboś 2025):** one pheromone blend carries both a **releaser** effect (immediate behavior) and a **primer** effect (slow physiological reprogramming) simultaneously — e.g. brood ester pheromone.

**Today:** the two are split across mechanisms — transient `Message` (releaser, TTL~30s) vs. the slow `HormonalState` channels (primer), which only the hypothalamus writes (hypothalamus.py:264–302). A cluster wanting both must emit separately.

**Change:** let a single `Message` carry an optional primer.

- Add `primer: dict[str, float] | None = None` to `Message` (bus.py:20) and thread it through `Message.hop` (bus.py:29) — backward compatible (default None).
- `Bus` accumulates primer nudges on publish into `self._pending_primers: dict[str, float]` (toggle-gated); `drain_primers() -> dict` returns and clears them. (Mirrors the Phase-2 accumulator design and keeps hormonal writes centralized.)
- Hypothalamus `process()` calls `bus.drain_primers()` once per turn and applies `self._bus.hormonal.add(ch, v * colony_primer_gain)` — so primer effects flow through the single existing hormonal-writer.

**Implication:** any cluster can deposit a slow physiological nudge alongside a fast signal in one emission, the way real chemistry does — without each cluster getting direct hormonal-write access. Risk: runaway hormonal drift if many messages carry primers; the `colony_primer_gain` scale and `HormonalState` clamps bound it. Off ⇒ `primer` ignored, drain never called.

---

## Phase 4 — Recruitment amplification *(`brain/bus.py` + cluster `_chem_snapshot`)*

**Biology (Ramírez-Moreno et al. 2025):** colony defense is detection → recruitment → attack, where alarm pheromone is the **recruitment amplifier**: a detection lowers nearby responders' thresholds in proportion to need, so the collective response scales with the signal.

**Today:** chemistry can *raise* thresholds (GABA caution) but there is no positive "recruit a cluster for collective response" primitive. `effective_threshold` (neuron.py:39) deliberately reads only the chemistry snapshot, not the bus.

**Change:** model recruitment as *just another channel in the snapshot* — zero new firing logic.

- `Bus` tracks a decaying recruitment level (same decay machinery as Phase 2): `recruit(cluster, level)` raises it; `recruitment_level(cluster) -> float` reads it (with `"*"` for global).
- In each cluster's once-per-turn `_chem_snapshot()` (see `brain/clusters/temporal.py:399`): when toggle on, inject `snapshot["RECRUIT"] = bus.recruitment_level(self.CLUSTER)`.
- Recruitable switches declare `modulators={"RECRUIT": -coeff}`. Because `effective_threshold` shifts by `coeff*(level-0.5)`, a recruitment level >0.5 *lowers* their threshold — they get recruited. Fully consistent with existing modulator semantics.
- A detector switch calls `bus.recruit(...)` (scaled by `colony_recruit_gain`) on high-salience detection.
- **Combines with Phase 5 in Phase 7:** recruitment is the dial that sweeps across the threshold-diverse population; threshold diversity makes the positive feedback graded and self-limiting. See Phase 7 for the unified cascade and the generalization beyond threats.

**Implication:** collective responses that scale with signal strength, expressed entirely through the existing modulator/`effective_threshold` path — `RECRUIT` is one more channel name. Risk: positive-feedback firing storms; bound by the decay half-life, the `[min_threshold,max_threshold]` clamp already in `effective_threshold`, and `modulation_gain`. Off ⇒ `RECRUIT` never enters the snapshot, so all existing modulator math is untouched.

---

## Phase 5 — Threshold diversity as division of labor *(`brain/neuron.py` + cluster construction / persona config)*

**Biology (Ramírez-Moreno et al. 2025):** given the *identical* alarm pheromone, the fraction of bees that responded by stinging ranged from ~0% to 83% across colonies. Individual response-threshold *variance* is what produces guards vs. soldiers vs. bystanders — specialization is a designed feature of threshold spread.

**Today:** switch thresholds are mostly uniform defaults (`threshold=0.5`); the 5 personas differ in *chemistry* but not in *response-threshold distribution*.

**Change:** deterministic, persona-seeded threshold spread, plus a 3-stage assignment convention.

- Helper `spread_threshold(base, persona_seed, switch_name, spread) -> float` in `neuron.py`: deterministic offset (hash of persona+name → bounded jitter within `±colony_threshold_spread`), so it's reproducible in eval (no RNG).
- Apply at switch construction when toggle on, guided by the detection→recruitment→action pattern: detectors lower, recruiters mid, action-stage higher — so the population self-sorts into roles.
- This is the most "design-principle" of the five and the lowest-risk: deterministic, bounded, reproducible.
- **Two axes of spread:** *within-cluster* (the detector→recruiter→action staging above) and *inter-cluster* (whole clusters given different baseline eagerness — e.g. a cautious persona's `motor` cluster high-threshold, its `caution`/hypothalamus low). The inter-cluster axis is a *static structural* bias and is largely orthogonal-but-redundant with persona **chemistry**, which already differentiates clusters *dynamically* via `modulators`/baseline neuromod. Treat inter-cluster spread as an optional fine-tuning knob layered under existing persona chemistry, not a replacement for it.

**Implication:** personas gain distinct *who-fires-first* personalities on top of distinct chemistries, and the colony gets robust division of labor for free (the bee result is the evidence). The low→high spread is also what Phase 7's recruitment cascade sweeps across, and what makes that positive-feedback loop self-limiting. Risk: thresholds drifting into never-fire/always-fire — bounded by `min_threshold`/`max_threshold` and the small `spread`. Off ⇒ uniform thresholds as today.

---

## Phase 6 — Silence-triggered recall (concentration × memory) *(`brain/dmn.py`; depends on Phase 2)*

**Idea (user) / biology:** tie the Bus concentration model into the memory systems so that *silent periods trigger recall* of information associated with prior high-concentration windows. This is hippocampal **replay during quiescence**, mediated by the **default-mode network** — exactly what the DMN already models. A lull on a recently-hot topic is not dead air; it's the system's chance to consolidate and free-associate around what just mattered.

**Today (verified — most of this already exists):**
- The DMN runs an idle loop (dmn.py:1352) and already has a **prefetcher** that calls `hippocampus.recall()` proactively every 4 ticks with a `{"topic","reason"}` signature (dmn.py:2197–2247) and a random-episode memory-seed path (dmn.py:1773–1810).
- Recall is semantic (768-dim cosine over `Episode` records, each storing a `neuromod_snapshot` at encode time — store.py:33) plus schema/tag/entity strategies (hippocampus.py:145–288), and returns a `recall_affect` dict that nudges ACh/GABA (hippocampus.py:248–267) — so recall already feeds back into chemistry.
- Rumination is idle-only and chemistry-driven (dmn.py:1611). **What's missing is only the silence→recall *cue*.**

**Change — a new DMN trigger, reusing the existing recall path:**

1. **New DMN sub-step** (toggle on): each idle tick, for each Phase-2 *armed* topic, check `bus.is_quiet(topic)`. On a fresh `ARMED→QUIET` edge (debounced, fire-once per quiet onset), build a recall cue from the Phase-2 **associated-context ring** for that topic — its captured tags/entities form the `query`/`entities`, and the captured neuromod snapshot can bias retrieval.
2. **Issue recall via the existing path:** publish to `mem.recall` (the topic hippocampus already subscribes — wiring_bootstrap.py:86) with the cue plus a new `silence_trigger: True` field, OR call the prefetcher's existing `hippocampus.recall()` route directly (dmn.py:2216). Recalled episodes flow back through `recall_affect` and can seed a `stream.thought` (the monologue already accepts memory seeds, dmn.py:1866) — so the recall surfaces as a reflective idle thought, exactly the intended "free-associate during the lull."
3. **Guards:** debounce so a topic that flickers quiet/active doesn't spam recall; respect the existing DMN skip-probability and rumination depth caps; only fire when OS-idle (reuse `get_idle_seconds`, utils.py:10) so it's genuinely a quiet period, not mid-exchange. Scope to the same armed channel(s) as Phase 2 (threat first), widening as Phase 2 generalizes.

**Implication:** quiet becomes *generative*, not just a stand-down — a topic cooling off pulls up what surrounded it while it was hot, recolors the entity's chemistry via `recall_affect`, and can voice itself as an idle reflection. It reuses the entire existing recall+DMN stack; the only genuinely new code is the QUIET-edge detector and the cue built from the Phase-2 context ring. Risks: recall churn during choppy activity (→ debounce + OS-idle gate), and recall loops (→ the DMN's existing multi-gate dedup, report §2, already blocks repeated thoughts). Off ⇒ no new trigger; Phase 2 off ⇒ nothing armed, so this is inert.

---

## Phase 7 — Graded mobilization cascade (recruitment × threshold diversity) *(synthesis of Phases 4 & 5)*

**Idea (user) / biology:** recruitment amplification (Phase 4) and threshold diversity (Phase 5) are one mechanism, not two. This is the **response-threshold model of division of labor** (Bonabeau/Theraulaz) and the bee defense cascade (Ramírez-Moreno et al. 2025): a need lowers response thresholds across a diverse population, so **low-threshold specialists fire first, their activity amplifies recruitment, and progressively higher-threshold reserves mobilize only as the need escalates.** Recruitment is the dial; the threshold distribution is the population it sweeps across. And the key stability property — **threshold diversity makes the positive feedback safe**: because high-threshold neurons demand strong recruitment, the cascade is graded and self-limiting (recruits in proportion to need, stalls when met) rather than the explosive all-or-nothing storm a uniform population would give under positive feedback. Diversity is the damper, not a complication.

**Generalization (user's "not just threats"):** recruitment is **task-typed resource mobilization**, not a defense-only primitive. Different needs recruit different specialists:
- a hard/ambiguous query → recruit more `frontal` drafters (more parallel attempts);
- a memory-laden turn → recruit deeper `hippocampus` recall (wider fan-out — note hippocampus already has chemistry-gated recall budget, hippocampus.py:182);
- sustained threat → recruit `caution` switches (the Phase-2 quorum feeds this);
- high novelty → recruit broader temporal processing.

**Change — a thin policy layer over Phases 4 & 5 (no new firing mechanics):**

1. **Reuse the Phase-4 primitive unchanged:** `bus.recruit(target_cluster, level)` raises a decaying per-cluster recruitment level; the cluster's `_chem_snapshot()` injects it as the `RECRUIT` channel; recruitable switches declare `modulators={"RECRUIT": -coeff}` and so lower their thresholds via the existing `effective_threshold`. Nothing new in `neuron.py`.
2. **Reuse the Phase-5 distribution unchanged:** `spread_threshold` gives each cluster a low→high threshold spread, so a rising `RECRUIT` level sweeps in responders in threshold order — a built-in first-responder → reserves ordering.
3. **Add a small recruitment-policy map** (settings-driven, toggle-gated): `need_signal → (target_cluster, recruit_gain)`. Need signals are quantities already computed each turn — query difficulty / salience / `requires_memory` (temporal features), Phase-2 threat quorum, surprise/novelty (predictor). A detector emits `bus.recruit(target, need_level * gain)`.
4. **Self-limiting by construction:** the recruitment level decays (Phase-2 half-life) and is clamped via `effective_threshold`'s `[min_threshold, max_threshold]`; as recruited responders satisfy the need, the need signal falls and recruitment relaxes. No explicit governor needed, but log the recruitment level + count-recruited each turn so a runaway is visible.

**Implication:** the system gains *proportional collective response* — it spends more cognitive resources (drafters, recall depth, caution) exactly when a need is strong, and idles them otherwise, with the cost scaling smoothly rather than flipping. This is the most "colony-as-organism" behavior of the set: graded mobilization with self-limiting positive feedback, achieved purely by composing two already-built primitives plus a policy table. Risks: a mis-tuned `recruit_gain` could over-mobilize → bounded by decay + threshold clamps + telemetry; coupling between needs (recall recruitment raising frontal load) → start with one need→cluster pair (query-difficulty → frontal drafters) and add pairs incrementally. Off (or Phases 4/5 off) ⇒ no recruitment injected, inert.

---

## Phase 8 — Aggregate-state neuromodulation feedback *(`brain/clusters/hypothalamus.py` + `brain/bus.py`)*

**Idea (user) / biology:** the colony's pheromone field reflects its *overall state*, and that aggregate feeds back to modulate every member. Translate that to a feedback loop where **global neuromodulation adjusts based on aggregated cluster outputs**, not only on input appraisal — the colony sensing itself and re-tuning its own chemistry.

**Already covered (the user's second framing — no work needed):** "responsive to both immediate context *and* long-term state" is the existing dual-layer chemistry — fast `Neuromodulators` (immediate) over slow `HormonalState` (long-term) with cross-talk (bus.py:169–194). Phase 8 *feeds* this existing structure rather than adding a new timescale.

**Today:** neuromod deltas come only from the hypothalamus's appraisal of *temporal/sensory features* (sentiment/hostility/surprise/salience → DA/GABA/ACh/Glu/NE, hypothalamus.py:92–164). There is **no loop from system-wide cluster activity back into chemistry.**

**Change — a small, clamped feedback term (toggle-gated under `colony_features`):**

1. **Aggregate signal from data already on the turn trace** (no new instrumentation): firing volume (`fired_path` length), modulation pressure (`modulated_switch_count` / `suppressed_switch_count`, neuron.py records these), excitatory-vs-inhibitory balance, and Phase-2 topic concentration. Reduce to a few scalars: *arousal* (firing volume), *coherence* (convergence/agreement vs. conflict), *inhibition load*.
2. **Map to small neuromod nudges**, applied by the hypothalamus (the single chemistry-writer): high aggregate firing → Glu (arousal reflects effort); broad coherence → DA (things cohered); high conflict/inhibition → GABA; high novelty spread → ACh.
3. **Stability discipline (mandatory — this is a feedback loop):** drive it from the **prior turn's** aggregate (avoid within-turn runaway), small gain `colony_state_feedback_gain` (start tiny), clamp the total feedback contribution, and log it as its own decisions event so its share of each channel is auditable. Because it feeds the fast layer, the existing fast→slow coupling integrates it over time automatically — satisfying the "immediate + long-term" aim via existing machinery.

**Implication:** the architecture becomes genuinely self-referential/emergent — chemistry reflects not just what the user said but what the system is collectively doing (effortful, cohered, conflicted), which then re-tunes gating. This is the most emergent of all the phases and also the highest stability risk; it ships last, smallest-gain, behind the toggle, and only after Phases 2 & 7's feedback behavior has been observed to be well-behaved. Off ⇒ chemistry driven purely by appraisal as today.

## Consolidated implications

- **One mental model:** every feature reuses an existing primitive — decay (Neuromodulators), modulators (`effective_threshold`), centralized hormonal writes (hypothalamus), the decisions log, the settings pattern. No parallel subsystems.
- **Emergence shifts upward:** Phases 2 & 4 add genuinely colony-level (superorganism) behavior — quorum, silence, recruitment — that no single cluster decides. This is the "non-brain capability" framing made literal.
- **Silence becomes generative (Phase 6):** the concentration model is not just a detector — feeding `QUIET` transitions into the existing DMN→hippocampus recall path turns lulls into consolidation/free-association, the way rest-state replay works. It also makes Phase 2 earn its complexity, since the silence machinery now drives a visible behavior.
- **Learning gets a valence axis** (Phase 1) and the colony gets **specialization** (Phase 5) — the two together make the 5 personas diverge more sharply in both *what they learn* and *who acts*.
- **Proportional mobilization (Phase 7):** recruitment × threshold diversity compose into a graded, self-limiting resource cascade — the system spends drafters/recall/caution in proportion to need. Threshold diversity is the damper that keeps the positive feedback from exploding; this is the safety argument for introducing feedback loops at all.
- **Self-referential chemistry (Phase 8):** global neuromodulation gains a feedback term from the system's own aggregate activity, making the architecture emergent rather than purely stimulus-driven. It is the highest-risk loop, so it ships last, smallest-gain, off the *prior* turn's aggregate, after Phases 2 & 7 are observed stable. The existing fast→slow chemistry coupling already supplies the "immediate + long-term" timescales it feeds.

# Fix job failures + give the brain a real memory-of-conclusions and a unified active ledger

## Context

10 hours of Langfuse traces showed two problems. (1) The DMN generates thoughts that **loop on the same theme** (bee/colony biology → emergent design), each a fresh one-shot generation that concludes nowhere — so the same insight is re-derived and re-suppressed forever. (2) Every self-generated **job failed** with `[planner failed]` and a `spoken_summary` full of `<|im_start|>` ChatML tokens.

Investigation revealed the deeper issue behind (1): the brain has **no durable concept of what it knows or has concluded**, and its "open" work is **fragmented across files**:
- `open_questions.md` ("Open Questions & Projects") is a hand-maintained ledger of threads + questions + projects. The DMN *reads* projects from it ([dmn.py:1065](brain/dmn.py:1065) `set_projects_context`) but **never writes to it**.
- `self.md` has a *separate* `## Open Questions` section that **sleep** appends to ([sleep.py:689-705](brain/sleep.py:689)) — duplicating the concept.
- Sleep also computes `insights` (the closest thing to concluded knowledge) but **only logs them to `decisions` and discards them** ([sleep.py:716-723](brain/sleep.py:716)). Nothing is ever persisted as knowledge.

**Design decisions (from the user):**
1. `open_questions.md` stays the **single active ledger** (open threads + questions + projects); the DMN reads *and writes* it. Resolve the `self.md` duplication into it.
2. **Concluded knowledge lives in memory, not a file** — encoded into the episodic/semantic store so it resurfaces through normal recall, not a growing markdown blob.
3. The knowledge store is fed **brain-wide**: DMN-concluded threads, sleep `insights`, completed-job outcomes, notable turn learnings.
4. Manual projects are **auto-detected in conversation** ("work on X", "add this to your open threads") and appended to `open_questions.md`.

Two parts: A) fix the job infrastructure; B) the ledger + memory-of-conclusions redesign.

---

## Part A: Job-failure fixes (infrastructure)

Root cause confirmed by git timeline: all failed jobs ran **2026-05-30 ~13:06–14:22 local**; the commit moving the planner to Claude Haiku (`f7e0b25`) landed **21:53 local** — *after* every failure. At failure time the planner was on the local Qwen model, which was degenerating. The planner is now Haiku ([motor_cortex.py:243](brain/clusters/motor_cortex.py:243)), but the corruption bug is still live everywhere else.

### A1. Add ChatML stop tokens — *the root fix*
`_call_local` ([model_router.py:841-849](brain/model_router.py:841)) builds the Ollama `/api/chat` payload with **no `"stop"` field**, so Qwen2.5 never halts at `<|im_end|>` and spews `<|im_start|>` until `num_predict`. Add `payload["stop"] = ["<|im_end|>", "<|endoftext|>"]` (gate on Qwen/ChatML model family). Repairs the planner, the spoken_summary, and every DMN/sleep/metacognition/skill-selector cell at once.

### A2. Sanitize local output (defense in depth)
After `data["message"]["content"]` ([model_router.py:858-861](brain/model_router.py:861)) add `_strip_chatml(text)` to remove leaked `<|im_*|>`/`<|endoftext|>`/trailing `<tool_call>` fragments and collapse runaway repeats — so one bad response can't poison a record even if a model regresses.

### A3. RunPod fallback for the ResultReporter
`ResultReporter` ([follow_through.py:197](brain/clusters/follow_through.py:197)) is hardcoded `model="runpod"` with no fallback. On empty/garbage after sanitize, retry once on `haiku` (short, cheap, latency-tolerant). Optionally skip RunPod when `second_brain/runpod_heartbeat.json` is stale.

### A4. Verify a job completes end-to-end
No job has run since the Haiku switch. After A1–A3, enqueue one self-task and confirm: parseable plan, executed steps, clean `spoken_summary`, `success: true`.

---

## Part B: Unified active ledger + memory-of-conclusions

All non-motor by construction — mechanisms mutate `open_questions.md`, encode memories, or set a span output; none touch `self._self_task_q`. Reuses the existing `SchemaStore` primitives ([store.py:346](brain/second_brain/store.py:346) `upsert_section`, `aappend_fact` w/ dedup, `ensure_section` for boot migration) and the hippocampus encode path.

### B1. DMN reads *and writes* `open_questions.md` (the single active ledger)
- Give the DMN a `SchemaStore` reference (it already imports `SECOND_BRAIN_ROOT`; thread the store in via the constructor / wiring where the hippocampus is constructed). Add a small in-memory `self._active_threads` mirror loaded from the file at boot so steering is cheap.
- **Open a thread:** when a monologue thought poses a question/unfinished idea (new JSON field `open_thread:true`, or a `?`/uncertainty heuristic) and isn't a near-duplicate of an existing entry, append a bullet under a managed `## Open threads` section in `open_questions.md` via `upsert_section` (rewrite the section body, preserving existing bullets). Keep the hand-written Architecture/Philosophical/Projects sections untouched — only manage the threads sub-section.
- **Relational tagging (per the AI's own diagnosis — "specificity is what makes routing work").** Every thread/reflection carries, beyond a topic tag: `bears_on` (which work-item/project/domain it connects to — e.g. `task-prioritization`, `evolution-pipeline`) and `bearing` (what *kind* of bearing — e.g. `changes-prioritization`, `affects-measurement`, `suggests-feature`). The monologue emits these (B6); they're stored on the ledger bullet and copied onto the conclusion/pending episode tags. This is what makes B8 routing precise rather than fuzzy topic-match.
- **Advance a thread:** new field `advance_thread_id`; append/replace the matching bullet's progress note. A thought tagged as advancing a thread is **exempt from the cluster-saturation & repeat-angle dedup gates** ([dmn.py:2014-2034](brain/dmn.py:2014)) — pass `advancing_thread=True` the same way `exempt_seed` already bypasses self-similarity. Those gates are exactly what blocks sustained progress today; we allow depth on a *tracked* thread while still blocking *untracked* looping.
- **Resolve/retire:** field `conclude_thread_id` + a one-line `conclusion`; or auto-retire when `advances >= BRAIN_DMN_THREAD_MAX_ADVANCES` (≈4, mirrors the rumination cap at [dmn.py:1639](brain/dmn.py:1639)); or age-out by **tick-count/wall-clock** (not assumed continuous ticking — chemistry suppresses ticks). On resolve → run B2, then remove the bullet from the ledger.
- Cap the open-threads section (≈6 bullets); evict oldest-least-advanced when full.

### B2. Memory-of-conclusions (lives in memory, fed brain-wide) — confident vs uncertain
The DMN **already writes episodic memory** (`encode_idle_thought`/`encode_deferred_question` both call `self._episodic.encode`), so this is the same pattern with a new tag/source — plus a **certainty branch**.
- Add `Hippocampus.encode_conclusion(session_id, text, source, tags, embedding_fn)` modeled on `encode_idle_thought` ([hippocampus.py:487](brain/clusters/hippocampus.py:487)): build an `Episode` with `topic_tags=["conclusion","knowledge",source,*tags]`, `entity_response="[CONCLUDED] " + text`, high `surprise_score` (≈0.7) so it surfaces readily in vector recall. No new file/collection — resurfaces through the **existing** retrieval pipeline.
- **Certainty branch on resolution.** The monologue emits a `conclusion_confidence` (or `needs_confirmation:true`) alongside `conclude_thread_id` (B6). Then:
  - **Confident** → `encode_conclusion(...)` and retire the thread.
  - **Uncertain (wants to check with the user first)** → route through the **existing deferred-question pipeline** instead: `_append_deferred_thought(text, urgency="high", tags=[...])` ([dmn.py:1115](brain/dmn.py:1115)) **+** `encode_deferred_question(..., tags=["pending_conclusion", thread_id])` ([dmn.py:2156](brain/dmn.py:2156)). The thread does **not** retire — it moves to `status: pending_confirmation` in the ledger (B1). This reuses the surfacing machinery that already exists (`take_deferred_thoughts()` shows it on user return).
- **Promotion on confirmation.** When the user later answers a surfaced pending-conclusion (detected in the same conversational-intent path as B5 — affirm/reject), promote it: `encode_conclusion(source="confirmed")` + retire the thread on yes; on no/correction, either re-open the thread with the correction as a new advance, or drop it. Tagging the deferred question with `thread_id` is what lets the turn layer find and resolve the right thread.
- **Feed it brain-wide (confident path):**
  - DMN: confident thread resolution → `encode_conclusion(source="dmn")`.
  - Sleep: stop discarding `insights` — route [sleep.py:716-723](brain/sleep.py:716) `insights` through `encode_conclusion(source="sleep")` instead of log-only.
  - Jobs: successful job → one-line outcome `encode_conclusion(source="job")` (hook near `update_summary`, [session_turn.py:939-946](brain/session_turn.py:939)).
  - Turns: notable durable learning (high salience/surprise) → `encode_conclusion(source="turn")`, reusing the existing turn-encode gate signals so it's selective.
- **Close the loop (stop re-derivation):** on boot and periodically, recall recent conclusions (tag filter `conclusion`) and surface 2–3 in the monologue prompt under **"Already concluded — build on or move past these, don't re-derive."** This is what actually stops the colony loop: the conclusion becomes a prior to move past, enforced by prompt + recall rather than only by dedup distance.

### B3. De-fragment: redirect sleep's open-questions to the unified ledger
Sleep currently appends `open_questions` to `self.md`'s `## Open Questions` ([sleep.py:689-705,731](brain/sleep.py:689)). Redirect that write to the `## Open threads` section of `open_questions.md` (same `upsert_section` path as B1) so there is **one** active ledger. Migrate any existing `self.md` open-questions into the ledger once at boot via `ensure_section`/a one-shot migration, then drop the `self.md` section.

### B4. Steer rumination toward the ledger
Change `_current_seed` ([dmn.py:1648](brain/dmn.py:1648)) so that when threads are open, rumination seeds from the **least-advanced / highest-priority open thread**, not blindly `_recent_thoughts[-1]`. Wire `_run_rumination` ([dmn.py:1654](brain/dmn.py:1654)) so its synthesized output calls advance-thread; when `_consecutive_ruminations` hits its cap, resolve+conclude that thread (B2). Rumination becomes the "make progress, then retire" engine.

### B5. Conversational intent: manual projects + pending-conclusion confirmation
Add lightweight intent detection in the turn/frontal task path (reuse the existing task-intent classifier in [follow_through.py](brain/clusters/follow_through.py) / `frontal_task.py`):
- **Manual project:** "work on X" / "add this to your open threads" / "new project: …" → append a project bullet to `open_questions.md` under `## Projects assigned by Russ`, matching the existing `### name` + `**Task**` + `**Status**` format `set_projects_context` parses; confirm in the reply; then call `set_projects_context` with the refreshed file so the DMN picks it up immediately (refresh path exists at [session_setup.py:347](brain/session_setup.py:347), [brain_session.py:375](brain/brain_session.py:375)).
- **Pending-conclusion confirmation (B2):** when the brain surfaced an uncertain conclusion (a deferred question tagged `pending_conclusion:<thread_id>`) and the user's reply affirms/corrects/rejects it, resolve the matching thread: affirm → `encode_conclusion(source="confirmed")` + retire; correct → re-open the thread with the correction as an advance; reject → drop the thread. Match on the `thread_id` carried in the deferred-question tags.

### B6. Monologue prompt steering + JSON fields (`dmn_prompts.py` `MONOLOGUE_SYSTEM`, [dmn_prompts.py:3-214](brain/dmn_prompts.py:3))
- Inject **OPEN THREADS** (from the ledger) + **Already concluded** (from memory recall, B2) context blocks near the existing "last few thoughts" assembly ([dmn.py:1842](brain/dmn.py:1842)).
- Add guidance: *"You are not only generating novelty — you are making progress. Most ticks should ADVANCE an open thread or CONCLUDE one that's reached a real conclusion. Open a new thread only when genuinely starting a new line. A thread you keep circling without concluding is the failure mode."*
- Extend the JSON schema ([dmn_prompts.py:204-214](brain/dmn_prompts.py:204)) with `open_thread:false`, `advance_thread_id:""`, `conclude_thread_id:""`, `conclusion:""`, and `conclusion_confidence:"confident"|"uncertain"` (drives the B2 branch — uncertain conclusions become a deferred question to the user rather than a silent memory write). Add prompt guidance: *"If you've reached a conclusion but aren't sure it's right, set conclusion_confidence:'uncertain' — it will be raised with the user before being treated as known, rather than committed as fact."* Parse in `_run_monologue` ([dmn.py:1916-1945](brain/dmn.py:1916)), independent of `task`/`propose`/`plan` so a thought can advance a thread *and* stay purely cognitive.

### B7. Langfuse observability
Add `outcome: dict | None = None` to `record_thought` ([timeline.py:598-624](brain/observability/timeline.py:598)) and set `output=outcome` before `span.end()` — `{action: opened_thread|advanced_thread|concluded|proposed|spoke|deferred|none, thread_id, conclusion?}`. The caller ([dmn.py:2069-2076](brain/dmn.py:2069)) already knows the action. Keep inside the existing try/except so observability never breaks the loop.

### B8. Relevance routing into live work + close-the-loop-on-use (the AI's "memory without momentum" fix)
The reframe from the AI: the bottleneck isn't storage, it's **routing** — good thoughts sit in a passive queue and never *land* anywhere that changes how work happens, so the same insights recur (exactly the colony-loop symptom). Three mechanisms, all on **existing rails**:
- **Surface at the moment it matters (into live turns, not just idle).** `hippocampus.recall` already pulls tag-filtered `deferred_episodes` into the live turn ([hippocampus.py:215](brain/clusters/hippocampus.py:215) → [session_turn.py:286](brain/session_turn.py:286)). Extend it to also recall open threads + pending reflections, **boosted when their `bears_on` tag matches current activity** — the active project digest (`self._last_projects` / `set_projects_context`) and the current turn's `features` (topic/entities). Inject the top 1–2 alongside `prefetched_context` ([session_turn.py:419](brain/session_turn.py:419) → [frontal.py:1576](brain/clusters/frontal.py:1576)) so a relevant unfinished thought shows up *while you're working on the thing it bears on*, without anyone hunting for it.
- **Close the loop on use.** When an injected thread/reflection is part of the context that shaped a response (we know what `recall` returned and what frontal injected), emit a `landed`/`used` event for that thread_id → mark it **resolved-by-use** in the ledger (distinct from DMN-concluded) and `encode_conclusion(source="landed")` so the realized insight becomes durable knowledge. This is the AI's "you stop carrying unresolved ideas as background load" — and it's the strongest anti-recurrence signal, because a thought that *did its job* is provably done.
- **Relevance ranking.** Routing uses the `bears_on`/`bearing` tags (B1) for precision; fall back to vector similarity when tags don't match. Bound surfacing (1–2 per turn) so live context isn't flooded.

This subsumes the earlier "surface concluded into the monologue prompt" (B2) idle-side surfacing and adds the missing live-side routing the AI is asking for.

### B9. Adaptive, self- and user-state-aware routing (the AI's "the loop should learn its own tuning" + "read the user's state")
Make B8 routing self-tuning, focus-respecting, and **protective of the user** — all through **existing brain machinery**, not a new ML layer.
- **Learn relevance from use/ignore (Hebbian).** The `landed`/`ignored` outcome from B8 is a reinforcement signal. Feed it through the existing `HebbianUpdater`/wiring graph ([hebbian.py:15](brain/hebbian.py:15), `wiring.get_edge_weight` / edge updates): reinforce the association between a `bearing`-type + activity-context and a successful surface (used), gently depress it when surfaced-and-ignored. Reuse the existing arousal/intensity **plasticity modulation** ([hebbian.py:62-122](brain/hebbian.py:62)) so emotionally salient "that landed" moments teach more strongly. The router then ranks/thresholds future surfacing by these *learned* weights instead of fixed rules — so routing sharpens toward what actually matters to this user over time. Apply at the same cadence Hebbian already runs (per session, [hebbian.py:221](brain/hebbian.py:221)).
- **Graceful degradation under the AI's own focus (chemistry gate).** Gate live surfacing on the **same ACh/attentional-engagement signal that already suppresses the DMN** ([dmn.py:1301](brain/dmn.py:1301)) plus turn cadence. High focus → hold matched threads rather than inject; release at a lull (low ACh / idle / topic shift). Reuse the idle-gate + chemistry snapshot the DMN already consults. Backoff, not silence — nothing dropped, only deferred.
- **Read the *user's* state → modulate surfacing volume (protective, not just productive).** Build a lightweight **user-load estimate** from signals the brain already tracks: message **terseness/verbosity trend** (parietal `user_style` / `_measure_verbosity`, [parietal.py:64](brain/clusters/parietal.py:64)), **turn pace** (cadence from the conversation tracker's `recent_turns`/timing), **task-switching vs locked-in** (topic/entity volatility across recent `features`), and **estimated user emotion/stress** (hypothalamus user-emotion estimate, carried on `Episode.user_emotion`). Map this to a per-turn **surfacing budget** (0–2): when the user is stretched (terse + fast + switching, or stressed) the budget drops toward 0 and matched threads are *held*; when they finish something or shift gears (a natural boundary) the held queue is **released when it won't cost them**. The objective is explicitly *surface useful ideas at moments the user can use them*, not maximize how many surface — one creates ambient pressure, the other creates value.
- The payoff (the AI's framing): the loop gets better the longer it's used, flexes with how work actually happens, and protects the user's attention instead of taxing it.

---

## Sequencing
1. **A1 → A2 → A4 (verify) → A3.**
2. B1 ledger read/write + thread lifecycle + relational tags → B2 `encode_conclusion` (confident/uncertain branch) + brain-wide feeds → B3 de-fragment sleep writeback → B6 prompt fields/parsing → B4 rumination steering → B5 manual projects + pending-conclusion confirmation → B8 live-work routing + close-the-loop-on-use → B9 Hebbian-learned + load-aware routing → B7 Langfuse outcome.
   - Note B9 depends on B8's use/ignore signal existing first; ship B8 with simple tag-match ranking, then layer B9's learned weights + focus gate on top.

## Verification

- **Part B memory:** unit — a `confident` conclusion calls `encode_conclusion` (episode recallable by tag `conclusion`) and retires the thread; an `uncertain` conclusion instead writes a deferred question tagged `pending_conclusion:<id>` + `_append_deferred_thought`, and leaves the thread `pending_confirmation`; an affirming user reply promotes it via `encode_conclusion(source="confirmed")` and retires the thread, a rejecting reply drops it. Sleep `insights` now produce conclusion episodes (not just logs); the monologue prompt contains the "Already concluded" block when recall returns conclusions.
- **De-frag:** assert sleep open-questions land in `open_questions.md`, not `self.md`; boot migration moves any legacy `self.md` entries once.
- **Manual project:** simulate "work on the Karaoke Hero review" → a `### …` project bullet appears under "Projects assigned by Russ" and `set_projects_context` picks it up.
- **Part B routing (B8):** unit — a turn whose `features` topic matches an open thread's `bears_on` tag surfaces that thread into `memory`/drafter context; once surfaced-and-used, the thread is marked resolved-by-use and an `encode_conclusion(source="landed")` episode is written; a non-matching turn does not surface it. Assert surfacing is bounded (≤2/turn).
- **Part B adaptive/load (B9):** unit — a `used` outcome reinforces the relevant routing weight and an `ignored` outcome depresses it (assert via `wiring.get_edge_weight` before/after); decay relaxes a stale weight toward rest; a high-ACh/deep-focus chemistry snapshot holds a matched thread (no injection) while a low-ACh/idle snapshot releases it; held threads age out at the next idle window. User-state: a stretched-user signal (terse + fast pace + topic-switching, or high estimated stress) drops the surfacing budget to 0 (held), and a task-completion/gear-shift boundary releases the held queue.
- **Behavioral (the real test):** replay the colony scenario through `_tick` with idle+rumination chemistry; assert the trace shows one thread opened → advanced → concluded → encoded to memory, and subsequent colony thoughts are suppressed *because the conclusion recall tells the model it's already concluded*. Then send a live turn on a related topic and assert the relevant thread is routed into the turn and marked resolved-by-use. Inspect `open_questions.md` and recall conclusions from the episodic store.

## Risks
- **Over- vs under-suppression flip:** exempting advancing-thread thoughts from cluster-saturation could reopen the loop the gate was added to stop. Mitigate with the hard advance cap and by requiring an explicit `advance_thread_id` (not heuristic match alone) for the exemption.
- **Ledger churn / clobbering hand edits:** only the managed `## Open threads` (and project appends) are machine-written; never rewrite the hand-authored Architecture/Philosophical/Efficiency sections. Use section-scoped `upsert_section`, not whole-file `awrite`.
- **Conclusion-recall noise:** tag-filtered recall must rank/limit (2–3) or the prompt fills with stale conclusions; bound how many are surfaced and prefer recent/high-surprise.
- **Chemistry gating:** thread advancement rides on `_tick` (gated by `idle_gate`/`_tick_skip_probability`); age-out must use tick-count/wall-clock or threads never retire during suppressed stretches.
- **Manual-project false positives:** auto-detect could mis-fire on casual mentions; require a reasonably explicit phrasing and confirm the write in the reply so the user can catch it.
- **Live-routing noise (B8):** surfacing threads into every turn could distract the response. Bound to 1–2, require a real `bears_on` match (not loose vector similarity alone), and let the existing speak/draft gates decide whether it's actually used — "used" is defined as *included in the context that produced the response*, not merely recalled.
- **Premature resolve-by-use:** a thread surfaced once shouldn't auto-resolve if it only got grazed. Gate resolution on the thread actually appearing in the selected draft's grounding (reuse the draft-selection signal), not on mere recall, so a thread isn't retired before it's genuinely landed.
- **Adaptive-routing instability (B9):** learned weights could overfit a few early signals or drift. Reuse Hebbian's existing **decay-toward-rest** ([hebbian.py:223](brain/hebbian.py:223)) so stale associations relax to baseline, keep learning-rate gentle (same scale as existing edge updates), and clamp weights so routing can't collapse to "never surface" or "always surface." Cold-start: fall back to B8 tag-match ranking until enough signal accumulates.
- **Held-thread starvation (B9 backoff):** under sustained focus, deferred threads could pile up and never release. Bound the hold queue and force a release/age-out at the next idle window (reuse the same wall-clock age-out as B1) so nothing is held indefinitely.
- **User-load misread (B9):** terseness/pace are noisy proxies — a curt message isn't always overload (the hypothalamus already cautions "short messages ≠ disengagement", [hypothalamus.py:76](brain/clusters/hypothalamus.py:76)). Use a *trend* across several turns, not a single message; bias toward holding (false-negative surfacing is cheaper than interrupting a stretched user); and never let user-state gating suppress a genuinely urgent/`immediate`-urgency item — those still go through the deferred-thoughts path.
- **Stop-token scope (A1):** correct only for ChatML models — gate on model family if non-Qwen local models are introduced.
